title: Unilateral morning glory disc anomaly in a patient with prenatal Zika virus exposure.
ehr_evidence: No electronic health record or database was used; data were collected from direct clinical ophthalmological examination, maternal real-time PCR testing, and pediatric neuroimaging (MRI and CT) as a single case report.
summary: A case report describing a 3-year-old male with confirmed prenatal Zika virus exposure who presented with unilateral morning glory disc anomaly and associated midline craniofacial and brain anomalies.
key_findings: First reported case of unilateral morning glory disc anomaly following confirmed prenatal Zika virus exposure.
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye.
Neuroimaging revealed a base of skull encephalocele through the floor of the sella and callosal dysgenesis.
The report explicitly states it cannot demonstrate a causal relationship between prenatal ZIKV exposure and MGDA.
No prior reports of MGDA in children with prenatal ZIKV exposure had been documented.
captured_features: Fundus photography findings (central funnel-shaped excavation, glial tuft, peripapillary atrophy, radial spoke-like vasculature OD)
Maternal RT-PCR-confirmed Zika virus infection in the second trimester
Brain MRI and CT findings (sellar encephalocele, callosal dysgenesis)
population: A single 3-year-old male pediatric patient evaluated at a pediatric ophthalmology clinic
limitations: Cannot establish causality between prenatal ZIKV exposure and MGDA.
data_availability_statement: All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this manuscript.
